findings_to_judge.finding: MMED's short interest is 5,896,696 shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement against a public float of 27.96m shares (Medtronic holds ~90% of 280.84m shares outstanding) - i.e. ~21% of float with 5.1-5.7 days to cover - yet the most widely syndicated short-interest pages display it as '2.1% of float' because they divide by shares outstanding rather than float; the position was built from 1,341,393 shares at the 2026-03-13 settlement to a 6,570,728 peak on 2026-06-30 and has been reduced only ~10% since, while the stock has roughly doubled off its 2026-05-15 low of $10.65.

The IPO lock-up lapses on the morning of the print: the 424B4 is dated 2026-03-05 and EDGAR full-text search confirms it contains the phrase '180 days after the date of this prospectus' (180 days from 2026-03-05 is 2026-09-01), and that lock-up binds Medtronic's ~252.9m shares as well as every officer and director; as of 2026-08-31 Medtronic's EDGAR submissions show no S-4, no Schedule TO and no 425 has ever been filed, so the split-off exchange offer is not launched and becomes launchable from this print forward against a stated intent to finish the separation in calendar 2026.

MiniMed's Senior VP, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, Courtney Nelson Wills, notified the company on 2026-07-30 that she is resigning effective 2026-09-25 after an eight-week transition - disclosed in an 8-K filed 2026-08-05, i.e. she departs inside the exact window in which a tax-free split-off exchange offer, an S-4 and ~160 Medtronic transition-services agreements have to be executed.

Q1 FY27 is a 14-week quarter and the two halves of the arithmetic sit in two different companies' disclosures: MiniMed's CFO said on 2026-06-03 that 'excluding the extra week, we expect Q1 growth to be roughly similar to Q4' (Q4 FY26 organic was 8.7%), while Medtronic's CFO quantified the extra selling week as '500 to 600 basis points to first-quarter growth' - stacking them implies MMED prints roughly 14% organic growth, versus the '~10% organic FY27 outlook' that quote pages and screens carry as the company's guidance.

MiniMed's fiscal Q1 FY27 is a 98-day (14-week) quarter — 2026-04-25 through 2026-07-31 — against a 91-day (13-week) prior-year quarter (2025-04-26 through 2025-07-25); the entire 53rd week of FY27 falls in this single quarter, and MiniMed's own definition of 'Organic Revenue Growth' adjusts only for FX and Italian payback accruals, NOT for extra weeks, so the organic-growth headline will print roughly double the 8.7% it printed for Q4 FY26 on calendar alone. The dates are established by the company's own filings: FY26 ended 2026-04-24 (Q4 exhibit 99.1), the year-ago quarter ended 2025-07-25 (Medtronic 10-Q mdt-20250725), and this quarter ends 2026-07-31 (the 2026-07-20 announcement).

The euro tailwind that supplied roughly half of Q4 FY26's reported-vs-organic gap (15.6% reported vs 8.7% organic) is gone in this quarter: EURUSD monthly averages for May/Jun/Jul 2026 were 1.1681/1.1510/1.1419 (avg 1.1536) versus 1.1276/1.1518/1.1698 a year earlier (avg 1.1497) — +0.34% y/y, against +8.2% y/y for the Feb-Apr window that Q4 FY26 covered. MiniMed's 10-K puts OUS revenue at ~70% of FY26 total (Q4 FY26: international $599m of $837m, US only $238m), making it one of the most FX-levered US-listed medtechs.

About $20m of Q4 FY26's $837m reported revenue was not product demand: the 'Other' line jumped to $22m from $2m a year earlier and the footnote defines it as 'net sales generated from the sales of smart insulin pens and services. Amounts in this line also reflect adjustments to the Company's Italian payback accruals' — a legal-accrual release that is expressly excluded from the organic growth definition. Anyone extrapolating the $837m base into Q1 has carried a one-off forward, and the underlying Italian exposure is live rather than settled: the Council of State (Ordinance No. 1589/2026) suspended industry appeals against the Ministry of Health decree of 29 December 2023 and referred the Medical Device Governance Fund to the Italian Constitutional Court.

The US business — the whole basis of the Flex equity story — grew 1.5% in Q4 FY26 ($238m of $837m) versus +12.2% organic internationally, and the reporting quarter cannot show the Flex inflection because Flex's actual differentiator arrived after quarter end: MiniMed's 2026-08-17 release says Flex 'now shipping' with Abbott's 15-day Instinct sensor, 17 days after the 2026-07-31 close, while the 2026-06-17 US launch release told customers the Instinct pairing was investigational and 'expected later in summer 2026'. The company therefore told prospective US pump buyers, inside the quarter, that a materially better bundle was weeks away.

Medtronic's April 2026 intrusion (ShinyHunters, unauthorised access 13-19 April 2026) resulted in notification of 3,834,294 individuals, with letters going out from late June into July 2026 — squarely inside MiniMed's fiscal Q1 — and several class actions already filed; exposed fields include Social Security numbers and health information. MiniMed filed its own Reg-FD 8-K on the incident on 2026-04-27 saying it was 'not aware of any compromises to the IT systems used by its business', but it has never quantified exposure, and the Q1 10-Q is the first periodic filing that must address it while MiniMed still runs on Medtronic IT under the separation arrangements.

Informative absence on the largest feared mechanical event: as of 2026-08-31 neither Medtronic (CIK 0001613103) nor MiniMed (CIK 0002062583) has filed a Form S-4, Schedule TO or Form 425 for the split-off exchange offer, so an exchange offer cannot legally launch in the days around this print, and Medtronic's FY27 EPS guidance still 'assumes consolidation of the Diabetes business for the full 12 months of FY27'. Separation groundwork is visibly proceeding but at governance pace, not offer pace — the board went from 9 to 11 on 2026-06-29 adding Alcon CEO David Endicott as an independent director, and the first annual meeting is set for 2026-10-09.
